newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends sharply down on milder US weather.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends sharply down on milder US weather.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed sharply lower on Monday as forecasts for higher temperatures in the United States compounded already-bearish sentiment in Europe generated by mild weather conditions, traders said.
Feb gas oil closed $6.75 a tonne lower at $209, off a session low of $208.50, having breached several support levels through the day.

"It was hovering around $3 to $4 down for most of the day and then slumped towards the end as (NYMEX) heating oil came off," a broker said. Heating oil was trading over one cent a gallon lower at when the IPE gas oil trade closed at 1730 GMT.
Temperatures on the U.S. East Coast and in the Midwest are expected to be above-normal this week, dampening heating oil demand.
Mild temperatures in Europe has dampened demand for heating oil barges in the ARA region, European physical traders said.
The March Brent/gas oil crack spread narrowed to $4.47.
March Brent was trading 24 cents up at $22.78 a barrel at 1805 GMT, off a session high of $22.91 as NYMEX crude retraced earlier gains.
"It didn't get up to (technical resistance) at $22.94, otherwise it might have gone higher," a dealer said.
Key technical support was pegged at $22.00.
